Ana, are you taking a table on Saturday? Dona Marta is closing the list tonight.
I want to, but I will decide on Friday. If the forecast is bad, I will not carry three chairs across a wet square.
You know it is never called off, whatever the sky does. If it rains before eight, we all move into the gym and that is that.
That is not really my problem. My problem is the varnish. If I do not get two dry days, the chairs will not be ready.
Then bring the small pieces and leave the chairs for next month. Nobody will notice.
And if I run out of time even for those? I have the vet on Friday afternoon.

Good evening, this is the recorded message for the Serra Verde fair. If you are calling about Saturday, here is everything you need to know. The forecast is not good, but the fair is going ahead. If it is raining before eight in the morning, we will set up inside the old school gym, and there will be a sign on the church door telling you where to go. If the rain starts later than that, we stay in the square and everybody covers their own table, so bring plastic. If you are a seller and you cannot make it, please call this number tonight, because if you do not tell us, we will hold your table until eleven and somebody else will lose the space. One last thing. If you are driving in from the main road, take the second entrance and not the first one. Chances are the first one will be flooded again.

People think that living out here means having endless free time, and it does not work like that at all. My whole weekend is a set of conditions. If I wake up and the sky is clear, I will be outside by seven, because the good light does not last. If it is raining, I will move into the workshop and do the sanding, which I can do in any weather. If a friend calls on short notice and says she is passing through, everything else gets postponed, and I do not feel bad about that anymore. The only rule I really keep is that if I run out of energy by four in the afternoon, I stop. I used to push through and then lose the whole of Sunday. So now, if the day is going badly, I will call it off early and start again the next morning. It sounds like a small thing, and it changed everything.

First, Tiago asks Ana whether she is taking a table at the fair on Saturday. Then Ana says that she will decide on Friday, when she sees the forecast. Next, Tiago reminds her that the fair is never called off, whatever the sky does. After that, Ana admits that her real problem is the varnish, which needs two dry days. Finally, Tiago offers her half of his own table if her pieces are not ready in time.
